chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: The piano-pushing opening and the dog jokes
summary: Green recites the opening to Rhythm For Sale: pushing the piano on stage, the stool gag and the wagon wheel and axle grease dialogue.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What did their show open up with?
Oh, they opened up with like, 'Rhythm For Sale.' They had a special song written for Buck and Bubbles.
Oh, it was a pretty thing. (Singing), rhythm mad 'All the world is a beautiful thing,' like that.
What singing, and then -- not tap dancing.

But it's music. The music would be playing it. The music. That's the instrumental. That's to bring them on. And you'd see the curtain shake or something, you know, and Bubbles would back out. 'Come on. Push on the piano.' The piano would move a little more. He'd say, 'That's it, push, push on the piano.' And you'd see Buck with the cap on, lean way out, and he's almost laying down, you know.
Trying to push a grand piano.
Yeah. He'd look out from under the cap at the audience and he'd say, 'Well, you just pull your end.'

And he'd say, "My end will follow." And he'd get out there and they'd be looking at each other you know, and the music stops. Buck would snatch the stool off the piano, and wind it, wind it down, you know. He'd sit it down in front of under the piano keys, the keyboard, you know. Then he'd sit down on the piano stool, you know, and he started talking. And like he'd ask him a question, "What's your name?" "How do they call you?" "You got a dog?" "Yeah, I got a dog." "What's his name?" He'd say, "I calls him wagon wheel." "Why do you call him wagon wheel?" "Because he knows when I spoke." He'd say, "You got a dog?" He'd say, "Yeah, I got a dog." "What's your dog's name?" "I ain't named him yet." He said, "What you going to call him?" He said, "I think I'll call him Axle Grease." He'd say, "Why are you going to call him Axle Grease?" He said, "Because he knows when I got the bones." And he says -- and he asked him something else. He'd say something else to him. He'd say, "You know what?" He said, "If you had in your head what I've got in mine, you couldn't sleep at night." He said, "I had them, but I got rid of them." He said, "Ha, ha, ha." He laughed. "You know what," he says, "You should pull your curtains down, your window curtains down." "Why should I pull my window curtains down?" He said, "Because I saw you kissing your wife last night." He says, "Oh, no, I wasn't even at home last night." Things like that. He'd throw his cap at him. No, no. When

he'd look over there he'd see Buck laying with his head on his forearm, you know. And he said, "What's the matter, are you tired?" He said, "No, I ain't tired." He's still got his head on his arm. He said, "Well, what you laying down there for?" Said, "Just resting, so I won't get tired." Then he'd throw his cap at him and hit him. So Buck raised up and he'd pick up his cap and pick up the piano stool, then he'd walk over to where Bubbles is standing, like he's going to hand him his cap back. So when Bubbles reached for his cap, he dropped it on the floor. He says, "There's your cap. Pick it up." And Bubbles would look at the piano stool he's holding, you see? He'd say, "That's not my old cap. That's my new cap." He'd say, "Well, pick up your new cap, where I can bust you across your old head." "You aren't going to hit me with that." "I'm going to knock all of the yarn off of you with this." He said, "You know, this ain't no ham sandwich I've got in this pocket." And he'd hold out the piano stool and say, "Yeah, and this don't look like no sponge cake, either." He said, "I'll cut that stool off and leave your hand up there." He said, "Put that down. Put that down." Buck would walk back to the piano keyboard and put the stool down. Then they'd get into (Inaudible). And he says, "Play some music."
